record.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
record.summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus that the utility says could require about 3,200 MW and allow up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. The program and contract terms are first-party/utility claims; the campus is not yet operating. A Georgia PSC filing shows consumer and environmental groups requested additional enforceable safeguards and disclosure for the redacted contract. The Georgia PSC docket page checked on 3 November still lists docket 44280 as open, shows no filing rows, and provides no result or order for the Oct 29 hearing. Actual curtailment, avoided infrastructure and customer savings remain unmeasured.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI announced the Grid Protectors program on 2 November 2026, describing a plan to develop future campus arrangements that reduce electricity use when local grids are under strain.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Georgia Power says a 25-year agreement for OpenAI’s planned Effingham County facility, which it expects to require about 3,200 MW, permits up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response during high-demand periods.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says it will pay the project’s full infrastructure and electric-service costs and describes the Georgia arrangement as a pilot for its Grid Protectors program; the campus is still in development.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In an August 2026 filing recorded by the Georgia PSC, NRDC, Sierra Club and Southern Alliance for Clean Energy asked Commission staff to object to the OpenAI contract unless enforceable protections cover costs and requested greater public disclosure; this is an advocacy filing, not a Commission finding.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected evidence does not establish actual curtailment, avoided generation or transmission investment, realized customer savings, the full terms of the redacted contract, or the Georgia PSC’s final disposition. On 3 November, the official docket page still listed docket 44280 as open, showed no filing rows, and no longer listed the 29 October hearing among upcoming events; it gave no hearing outcome or order.

evidence_gaps.description: The campus is planned and no operational curtailment magnitude, duration, frequency, reliability contribution or realized customer savings were inspected.

The current PSC docket page still lists docket 44280 as open, its filing table displays no records, and it provides no outcome or order for the Oct 29, 2026 trade-secret-access hearing. The complete agreement and Commission disposition remain unestablished; an August intervenor filing says terms were redacted and asks for further protections and public scrutiny.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as announced, large flexible compute loads could support grid reliability and alter infrastructure planning and cost allocation. The program is newly announced, but its cited campus is still planned and realized system or customer benefits are unmeasured.
limitations: The program’s expansion beyond the Effingham example is an announced plan, not delivered capacity.
The Effingham project remains in development; the claimed 1,000 MW is an agreed maximum, not demonstrated continuous curtailment.
OpenAI and Georgia Power describe full cost payment and customer benefits, while the agreement itself was not inspected in unredacted form.
The PSC rules describe protections for large loads generally, but the specific contract’s complete terms and final disposition were not established.
The August PSC filing is an advocacy request raising concerns; it is not evidence that the Commission found the contract inadequate.
The Georgia PSC docket page checked Nov 3 still lists docket 44280 as open and displays no filing rows or result for the Oct 29 hearing; a separate order/minutes record was not recovered.

technical.claimed_result: Georgia Power says the Effingham agreement permits up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response over 25 years for a planned facility expected to need about 3,200 MW. OpenAI says it will pay full project infrastructure and electric-service costs.
technical.demonstrated_result: OpenAI announced the program and Georgia Power published the cited agreement terms; no operating or measured result was inspected. The Georgia PSC docket page checked Nov 3 lists the matter as open, displays no filing rows, and provides no result or order for the Oct 29 hearing.
technical.implementation_status: Program announced; Effingham project is in development, and the agreement is subject to a Georgia PSC review context.
technical.mechanism: Demand response: the utility may reduce electricity delivered to the planned campus during specified high-demand periods; OpenAI also describes potential on-site generation/storage and power controls for future locations.
technical.regime: Planned OpenAI Effingham County campus served by Georgia Power; local agreement terms and future Grid Protectors arrangements may vary by site.
technical.reproducibility: No public operating data, full contract, independent cost allocation or measured load-curtailment results were inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable to the announced grid-flexibility agreement.

brief.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
brief.why_it_matters: Large compute campuses can create very large grid loads. A binding ability to curtail load could make some demand a system resource, while long-lived generation and transmission investments create cost-allocation and stranded-asset questions. The program’s value depends on the contract’s enforceable terms, deployment and measured grid outcomes.
